title: A New 'Super Team' of Countries Could Be Forming!
summary:
Have you ever made a pact with your friends to always stick together? That's kind of what three countries just did! Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan signed a new defense agreement called the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, or the Mecca Pact. It says that if any one of them is attacked, the others will treat it like an attack on all of them. It's like a superhero team-up!

Now Turkey's president, Recep Tayyip Erdogan, says Egypt might join too. He called the pact "open to further members" and said Egypt's participation is "possible." The deal was signed last Friday in the holy city of Mecca by Erdogan, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, and Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

Some people compare it to NATO's Article 5, which says an attack on one NATO country is an attack on all. But officials in Pakistan say it's not exactly like NATO and isn't aimed at any single country.

Erdogan also talked about other big issues in the region. He said reopening the Strait of Hormuz is a priority because its closure hurts everyone. He praised Qatar for helping with peace talks. He promised Turkey would support Syria, Gaza, and Lebanon. On Gaza, he said Turkey "cannot leave Gaza alone" and that Hamas is keeping its promises while Israel continues the war.

Erdogan also said the European Union doesn't seem to want Turkey as a member, and that's okay with him now. He said Europe would be "the loser." And he mentioned that former President Trump promised him F-35 fighter jets, but that's still waiting to happen because of a dispute over Russian missiles.
why_it_matters: This story matters because countries, like friends, make promises about protecting each other, and those promises can change who is safe, who is angry, and how world problems are handled.

background_read: Recep Tayyip Erdogan has been Turkey's president for many years and is one of the region's most powerful leaders.
Mecca, the city where the pact was signed, is in Saudi Arabia and is considered the holiest city in Islam.
NATO is a military alliance of many Western countries, and its Article 5 promise—an attack on one is an attack on all—is a famous example of collective defense.
Article_Structure: WHO: Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan—led by President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif—signed the agreement; Egypt might join later.
WHAT: They signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, also called the Mecca Pact, promising that an attack on one country will be treated like an attack on all of them.
WHERE: The deal was signed last Friday in the holy city of Mecca.
WHY: Erdogan says the pact is open to more members and not aimed at any single country, and it comes as he discusses regional issues like the Strait of Hormuz, Gaza, Syria, and Lebanon.

perspectives.description: They see the pact as a strong promise to protect one another and as a door open to new members like Egypt.
Some officials say the pact is not exactly like NATO and is not aimed at any single country, so it is about cooperation rather than making an enemy.
Others may worry that the pact shifts power in the Middle East and South Asia, especially because Erdogan also discussed Gaza, Syria, and Russia-related disputes.
